edge.title: The video that begs to be forwarded
edge.anchor: Bengaluru police arrested a man over an AI-generated video showing a blast at Vidhana Soudha, and filed an FIR (The Hindu, NDTV, Deccan Chronicle, 22 Oct).
edge.setup: A clip lands in a family or office group: smoke, a loud bang, a landmark you know. The caption says 'share before it is deleted' and 'media is hiding this'. Your thumb is already over the forward button.
edge.tell: A shocking clip with no named source, no outlet reporting it, and a caption telling you to spread it fast.
move: Stop before forwarding; a real blast in a city of this size is on several news sites and police handles within minutes.
Check one of: police or city police posts, or two established outlets. If neither carries it, treat it as fake.
Do not forward it even 'to warn people'; the person who shares it is on the record, and in this week's case the maker was arrested.
Tell the sender in the group that it is unverified and ask them to delete it.
edge.why: Fear makes the clip feel urgent, and urgency is what the maker is after: every forward is free distribution. AI tools now make convincing footage cheap, so 'it looks real' proves nothing. The reliable check is not the picture but whether independent sources you already trust carry it. Forwarding also puts your name on it.
edge.variants: Same shape: a fake 'bridge collapse' or 'riot' clip, a voice note claiming a water or fuel shortage tomorrow, a forwarded 'government order' about a bank or app shutting down.

lens.name: Loss aversion
lens.one_line: Losing ₹1,000 hurts about twice as much as gaining ₹1,000 pleases — and salespeople know it.
lens.detail: The same offer framed as a loss moves people far harder than framed as a gain, so persuasion is engineered to make inaction feel like losing something: expiring offers, 'you'll lose your spot', free trials that auto-convert once the thing feels yours. Noticing the frame restores the actual choice underneath it.
elsewhere: 'Only 2 left at this price' converting far better than a discount.
Holding a falling stock to avoid realising a loss.
Free trials relying on the pain of giving something up.
lens.test: Is this being framed as something I'd lose? Restate it as a plain gain and see if I still want it.
lens.today: Bengaluru police arrested a man over an AI-generated video of a blast at Vidhana Soudha (The Hindu, NDTV). Such clips work because they frame inaction as a possible loss: 'share now or someone gets hurt'. Restate it as a plain gain, 'I have confirmed this happened', and the urge to forward fades.
